Emma — thanks, this is a great, concrete ask. Below is a short, practical explanation and then I attached a worked example estimate based on your CSV. I kept legal/pricing exceptions for the contract team — Grace and Vivek are cc'd.

Quick rules (short):
- System messages: counted as input tokens. Any tokens that are part of the request sent to the model (system, user, assistant context) are included in input.
- User messages: counted as input tokens.
- Model-generated content: counted as output tokens. That includes the generated content returned by the model when it writes the assistant message.
- Tool/function responses: counted as output tokens when they are produced by the model (i.e., the text/JSON the model emits). If Redwood is calling an external tool on your behalf and the tool returns text that we then include in the assistant reply, those bytes are billed as output tokens.
- Function-call metadata (the wrapper tokens used to represent a function call — e.g., the special tokens that encode the call name/arguments on the wire) are treated as part of the request/response text and therefore fall on the input or output side depending on who "produces" them in the request turn. Practically speaking, the most important rule is: anything the model read counts as input, anything the model generated counts as output.

Rounding and aggregation (short):
- Tokenization: we use the model tokenizer to compute token counts; tokenization yields integer tokens (no fractional tokens).
- Billing aggregation: we sum token counts across all requests in the billing period and charge on the total. We do NOT apply an additional per-request up-rounding rule beyond the tokenizer output. In other words, there is no built-in per-call +10 token rounding in the hosted billing by default.
- Enterprise exceptions: for customers with many tiny requests, we can negotiate a billing normalization (for example, rounding to 10-token buckets or offering a per-request microbilling cap) as a contractual option. That is not the default but we can include it in a Dedicated/Private contract or as a custom line item for a committed spend.

Discounts and pilot pricing:
- Standard hosted rate (public ratecard): see attached redwood_ratecard_v3.pdf — for raw forecasting use that as the baseline.
- For a committed 12-month usage of ~10M tokens/month we typically offer tiered discounts starting at 10–15% depending on exact mix (generation-heavy vs embedding-heavy) and payment terms.
- For pilots we can offer $5k–$15k of credits plus an option to convert to committed pricing with a retroactive credit if you sign within 30 days.

What I attached: worked_estimate_10M.csv (counts rolled up to monthly totals) and a short note on contract options. If you'd like, I can convert the worked example into a single-line PO quote with the discount numbers included.
